cells.tense: You are in it now, and the choosing is still yours to make.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you actually mean to the connection in front of you, and let your yes be plain when it lands.
cells.core:
You meet what comes with your whole attention, and it meets you back. The direction isn't argued into place — you feel your way, and the feeling turns out to be right. What you already are keeps showing up, undistorted, in the way you take someone in.

Nothing is being forced here. The flow you're in runs because both sides keep saying yes to it, not because either side is gripping. Keep feeding it with the truth of what you notice, and it stays this alive. The sheet line is the one to carry: you're letting what you are speak, and it's being heard.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for a version of this that hasn't been written yet.
cells.ask: Before you reach for anyone today, let one finished thing sit unshared until it settles on its own.
cells.core:
You're dreaming the connection before it's here. You can feel the whole shape of it — how it will go, what it will mean — and you're living in that picture while the actual thing is still forming. You pull toward it faster than the moment can hold.

What you want isn't more vision. It's the rest vision grows from. Let one day finish before you build the next one out of it, and the pull softens on its own. That's the whole ask: let something be complete before you ask it to become.

The line to keep is close to this: you're building it before the ground under it has settled.

cells.tense: A crossing already happened and you're still standing at the side you left.
cells.ask: Say one true thing you've kept unsaid to the person across from you, and let their answer stand without correcting it.
cells.core:
You stopped meeting, and you can feel the room where the stopping started. Since then the pull toward someone else gets held at arm's length — watched, weighed, kept at the distance where it can't ask anything of you. What you see about the people near you is accurate. You just stopped letting it move you.

Nothing here needs a big gesture. Say one accurate thing about what you see, straight, to someone who can answer. Their answer will either land or it won't, and either way you're in the meeting again. Keep the line: you still see clearly — what went quiet is saying it out loud.

cells.tense: You are already the one setting the course here, and you keep calling it the situation.
cells.ask: Name one choice you've been describing as how things are, and say out loud that you made it.
cells.core:
You can stay yourself with someone and let that shape where the two of you go. When it's going well, you bring what you actually want into the room, and the other person gets to bring theirs, and the direction comes out of both — no one managing it, no one disappearing.

What's happening instead is quieter. You hold back here, go along there, bring this one close and keep that one at distance — and it all looks like it's just what's happening. The steering runs; you haven't called it yours. Nobody's asking you to freeze it. Pick one thing you've been treating as circumstance and say, plainly, that you decided it. That's today's move. The line: the course is already being set — just not yet claimed.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: that the person has one particular other in view. The card is a capacity, not a person, so I never name anyone or say who, how long, or what happened. The reader's likely objection: 'there's no one I'm choosing right now' — the cells survive because the mechanism is about how you meet what comes, not about a partner existing. The ask is useful even if the read is wrong: one plain yes, one thing finished before it's shared, one true sentence said straight, one choice named as yours — all of these move something regardless. Sentences that serve the writer more than them: any line implying the connection is already settled, and the noun-made-of-a-verb habits ('the reaching,' 'the knowing,' 'the choosing') that sound deep and say nothing; all cut.
